verdicts.trueWording: Ki'O society is divided into two halves or moieties, called
verdicts.note: 'Mountain Ways' headnote, first line: present-tense passive 'is divided', self-glossing 'moieties' as 'two halves'; raw HTML of ursulakleguin.com fetched with a browser UA (HTTP 200).

verdicts.trueWording: they aren't called anything, except sacrilege
verdicts.note: Headnote's last structural sentence names the two forbidden pairings (Morning woman/Morning man, Evening woman/Evening man) and ends on this clause. Every limb on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: In the stony uplands of the Deka Mountains the farmholds are
verdicts.note: First line of the story proper, immediately after the headnote; present-tense 'are', named upland (Deka Mountains), density stated in the clause that follows ('few and far between').

verdicts.trueWording: Danro is the farthest farm of Oro Village
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim; the sentence nests Danro / Oro Village / High Watershed / Mane River / Oniasu / O. Five levels are typed by the page, the fifth is not.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'continent' - the page never types Oniasu as a continent, only 'on Oniasu on O'

verdicts.trueWording: The farmers are dependent on the ariu; the ariu are not
verdicts.note: 'Mountain Ways', second paragraph: semicolon-joined two-clause reversal, in a paragraph about combing fleece and selling pelts, so the relation is economic on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: An addition to "POVERTY: The Second Report on Eleven-Soro"
verdicts.note: Headnote line under the title 'Solitude', continuing with the Mobile's name and 'by her daughter, Serenity'. Named report, ordinal 'Second', and Eleven-Soro identified later in paragraph 2 as the eleventh planet of the Soro system.

verdicts.trueWording: My mother, a field ethnologist, took the difficulty of learning anything
verdicts.note: Opening words of 'Solitude' paragraph 1; the bare apposition sits between the subject and the verb, so nothing is said of her before the profession.

Books & Boots introduces the block as the novel's opening quote from the 'Abridged Handy Pocket Guide to Intelligent Life-forms', 'which I quote in full'; heading carries area number, entry number, planet name. (The same post later calls the Semley story the novel's opening; the handbook entry is the epigraph before it.)

verdicts.trueWording: Highly intelligent, fully hominoid nocturnal troglodytes, 120-135 cm. in height
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim in the Species I-A entry, and the string is verbless. But it does not close there: the page continues the same string with two more items after the height.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'closing on a height range' - the string runs on past the height with 'light skin, dark head-hair'

verdicts.trueWording: Technology enhanced to Industrial, Point C, during League Mission of 252-254
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim in Species I-A; grade ('Industrial, Point C'), date range (252-254) and suppressed agent all on the page. The clause is not verbless: it is a reduced/non-finite clause built on the participle 'enhanced' (contrast the genuinely verbless line at index 786).
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'verbless clause' - the clause carries the participle 'enhanced'

verdicts.trueWording: indicated village and nomadic communal societies
verdicts.note: Species I-B entry: the sentence's subject is 'Brief contacts' (the blog's OCR renders it 'Brief con~ tacts'), and the entry closes 'Status E-Query', so the evidential grading is on the page.
Species I-B (the Fua), penultimate sentence of the entry; the post's later handbook block confirms taxation is an institutional category ('Control and Taxation Missions').

verdicts.trueWording: Four major landmasses... occupy 38% of planetary surface
verdicts.note: Second handbook block ('Number 62: FOMALHAUT II'), physical description, immediately after the gravity line; the four continents are named in between.

verdicts.trueWording: History: The planet was charted by the Elieson Expedition in 202
verdicts.note: Second handbook block: 'History:' labels the section whose remaining lines are the surveys and missions; first sentence is passive, dated 202, and names the expedition.

verdicts.trueWording: First Ethnographic Survey, 321, Director: G. Rocannon
verdicts.note: Last line of the second handbook block on the page: label, year, named director, no verb.
